# Patched torrent engine (librqbit 9.0.1)

These three crates are copies of librqbit 9.0.1 from crates.io with FluxDM's changes on top. `Cargo.toml`'s
`[patch.crates-io]` points the build at them. Every change is marked with a `FluxDM patch` comment, so
`grep -rn "FluxDM patch" vendor/` lists them all.

To upgrade librqbit: copy the new versions over these folders, then redo each change below. They're small
and self-contained.

| What | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Tracker status registry**: state, seeds, leeches, peers received, message, next announce for each tracker | `librqbit-tracker-comms/src/tracker_comms.rs` (`pub mod status`), `tracker_comms_http.rs` (`complete`/`incomplete` are `Option`) | The Trackers tab. librqbit parsed these numbers and threw them away. Reached through `librqbit::tracker_status`. |
| **Peer piece count and interest** (`pieces_have`, `peer_interested` on `PeerStats`) | `librqbit/src/torrent_state/live/peer/stats/snapshot.rs` | Seeds count, per-peer progress and flags. |
| **File priorities**: `ManagedTorrent::set_file_priorities(levels)` reorders the engine's file download queue (higher level first, then name), kept across pause and resume | `librqbit/src/torrent_state/mod.rs`, `torrent_state/live/mod.rs` (`set_file_levels`), `session.rs` | Low / Normal / High / Maximum, like the .NET version. librqbit already had the ordered list internally (by name only). |
| **Finished files held read-only** (`TorrentStorage::on_file_completed`, `OpenedFile::reopen_read_only`), applied when a file's last piece verifies, after the startup check and when a torrent goes live | `librqbit/src/storage/mod.rs`, `storage/filesystem/{fs,opened_file}.rs`, `torrent_state/live/mod.rs`, `torrent_state/initializing.rs` | Windows refuses programs that open a file for reading without sharing write access while anyone holds a write handle. Before this, finished torrent files couldn't be opened by many apps while FluxDM held them. librqbit had a comment saying this should happen. |
| **BEP 55 holepunch**: the `ut_holepunch` message, relay / initiator / target roles | `librqbit-peer-protocol/src/extended/ut_holepunch.rs` (new), `extended/mod.rs`, `lib.rs`; `librqbit/src/torrent_state/live/mod.rs` (`on_holepunch`, `try_holepunch`, `holepunch_connect`), `peer/mod.rs` (`supports_holepunch`), `stream_connect.rs` (`prefer_utp`) | Reaches peers behind NAT/CGNAT through a peer both sides are connected to; the .NET build's MonoTorrent fork had it. When a direct dial to a peer learned over PEX fails, FluxDM asks that PEX source to introduce them. Both sides then dial uTP at the same moment. Counters: `librqbit::holepunch_stats`. |
| **Availability**: `TorrentStateLive::availability()` gives distributed copies of the still-needed pieces among connected peers | `librqbit/src/torrent_state/live/mod.rs` (`needed_pieces`, `availability`) | The Availability column. Below 1.00, some needed piece isn't on any connected peer. |
| **Seed-first peer turnover** (replaces the .NET-fork port): every 5 s, while downloading with 80%+ of slots full and peers waiting, drop up to 8 of the worst connections - leechers with nothing we need, then slow leechers, then idle or slow seeds (under a quarter of our best peer's speed); fast peers of either kind are kept. Per-torrent connection limit default 100 -> 200 (`src/torrent.rs`) | `librqbit/src/torrent_state/live/mod.rs` (`turnover`, `pick_turnover`, `PeerSeen`, `task_peer_turnover`, `turnover_tests`) | On ADSL our upload is small; leechers want it while seeds give their full speed for free. Slots go to the fastest seeds. |
| **PEX shares incoming peers too, with BEP 11 flags** (seed / uTP / holepunch / reachable) | `librqbit-peer-protocol/src/extended/ut_pex.rs` (`from_addrs_with_flags`), `librqbit/src/torrent_state/live/mod.rs` (`pex_candidates`) | librqbit only shared peers it had dialed itself, so peers behind NAT (which only connect in) were never shared. Those are the peers hole-punching is for. |
| **Live speed limits**: `ManagedTorrent::set_ratelimits` changes a running torrent's own limits; `Limit::set` ignores an unchanged value | `librqbit/src/limits.rs`, `torrent_state/mod.rs`, `torrent_state/live/mod.rs` | Changing a limit used to remove and re-add the torrent (a full disk re-check), and re-setting the session limit every second rebuilt its bucket, so the cap leaked a burst each second. |
| **Sequential download**: `ManagedTorrent::set_sequential(bool)`; `ChunkTracker::iter_queued_pieces` walks each file from its first piece to its last when it is on (an `AtomicBool` in `ManagedTorrentOptions`, read on every piece request, so it can be flipped while running) | `librqbit/src/torrent_state/mod.rs`, `torrent_state/live/mod.rs` (`acquire_next_piece`), `piece_tracker.rs` (`set_sequential`), `chunk_tracker.rs` (`iter_queued_pieces`), `session.rs` | "Download in order" in the torrent menu. Stock librqbit always picks first, last, then the middle of each file. |
| **Slow limits and "No upload"**: the limiter bucket holds at least 32 KB (`MIN_BURST`); an upload limit of 1 B/s sets `Limits::upload_blocked`, and `task_upload_scheduler` drops requests while the torrent's or the session's upload is blocked | `librqbit/src/limits.rs` (`is_block`, `upload_blocked`, `fluxdm_tests`), `torrent_state/live/mod.rs` (`task_upload_scheduler`), `src/tests/e2e_no_upload.rs` (new) | Governor refuses to pass more than one bucket at once, and the bucket was one second's worth: under 16 KB/s no 16 KB block could ever pass, the error ended the upload task, and uploads stayed dead even after the limit was raised. The app therefore raised every limit to 32 KB/s, so "No upload" and 20 KB/s both uploaded at 32 KB/s. |

| **Force announce without a disk check**: `ManagedTorrent::force_announce()` wakes every HTTP/UDP tracker independently, interrupts HTTP retry backoff, and refreshes DHT/local discovery while retaining live state and peers; private torrents keep discovery disabled | `librqbit/src/session.rs`, `torrent_state/mod.rs`; `librqbit-tracker-comms/src/tracker_comms.rs` | Manual reannounce previously removed and re-added the torrent, triggering a disk check. Automatic tracker intervals remain in effect between manual requests. |
| **Check selected pieces only**: initial checks skip unselected-only pieces, include boundary pieces, and report selected/sample checking bytes; resume samples discard unselected claims and reject hash mismatches | `librqbit/src/file_ops.rs`, `torrent_state/initializing.rs`, `torrent_state/mod.rs` | Unticked files should not be read in full; a failed sample must invalidate resume data. Boundary data uses the filesystem part-file routing described below. |
| **Durable resume data**: pause and completion synchronously persist the bitfield, queued older snapshots cannot overwrite it, low-speed transfers flush every 60 seconds, initial/recheck snapshots sync before publication, and shutdown saves paused intent; detach for unchanged moves/tracker edits retains verified bits | `librqbit/src/bitv.rs`, `session.rs`, `session_persistence/json.rs`, `torrent_state/live/mod.rs`, `torrent_state/mod.rs` | Small transfers lost resume progress before the 16 MB threshold. Already-paused torrents still need persistence, and pause during checking must not transition back to downloading. |
| **Unwanted-file part storage**: selection reaches storage before initialization; unselected reads/writes use torrent-global offsets in a sparse `.fluxdm.parts/<info-hash>` file. Selection changes migrate retained bytes under a routing lock; promotion publishes a synced temporary file atomically. Pause handoff retains routing and handles; removal deletes only that hash's part-file, while detach for recheck/move preserves it. Storage wrappers forward selection/removal. The directory is hidden on Windows and reserved against torrent filenames. | `librqbit/Cargo.toml`, `src/storage/mod.rs`, `storage/filesystem/{fs,mod,opened_file,sparse}.rs`, `storage/middleware/{slow,timing,write_through_cache}.rs`, `session.rs`, `torrent_state/{mod,paused,live/mod}.rs` | Unticked files used to be created for boundary pieces. Hash-specific files inside the hidden directory support torrents sharing an output folder. Previously downloaded files moved out of the selection keep their bytes in parts; later selection restores them. |
| **Pause handoff and deferred restore**: pause waits for live task cleanup and disk-check completion; waiting checks wake on pause, completion publishes under the state lock, and deferred restoration leaves disk paths untouched while retaining resume data and unique persisted IDs | `librqbit/Cargo.toml`, `session.rs`, `session_persistence/json.rs`, `torrent_state/{mod,initializing,live/mod}.rs` | Immediate resume must not overlap old peer callbacks or leave a stopped check running. The application checks for missing wanted files before opening storage. Tokio task tracking requires the rt feature. |

Tested on 2026-10-01:
- **Unit tests:** the engine's own suites pass (librqbit 32, peer-protocol 23 including the new `ut_holepunch` codec test, tracker-comms 4).
- **Live swarm:** tested on the Debian 13.7 netinst swarm. Seeds were counted, per-peer speeds and progress showed, and the tracker reported Working.
- **Hole-punch interop:** relays running other clients answered our rendezvous requests with `connect`.
- **File locking:** files of a finished, loaded torrent open with `FileShare.Read`. They were "in use" before.

Tested on 2026-10-26 (limits patch): the engine's suites pass with the patched siblings (librqbit 36, including the
new `limits::fluxdm_tests` and `tests::e2e_no_upload`). `e2e_no_upload` runs a local seeder with upload blocked:
the downloader gets 0 bytes in 8 s while the seeder's torrent stays Live, then completes once the limit is lifted.
The same test against the unpatched engine fails: the seeder never uploads again after the limit is lifted.
Run them from a copy of `vendor/` with a `[patch.crates-io]` for `librqbit-peer-protocol` and
`librqbit-tracker-comms` pointing at the sibling folders (testing in place would rewrite `librqbit/Cargo.lock`).

Tested on 2026-10-30 (torrent reliability): application regression tests use read-counting storage,
local HTTP/UDP trackers, persistent sessions and an in-process TCP seeder/leecher. They cover selected
boundary reads, unchanged live state after reannounce, pause during checking, resume sampling on restart
and move, full explicit recheck, corrupted resume samples, and durable small-transfer pause/completion.
No external swarm or real user data is involved.

Tested on 2026-10-30 (part-file storage): three application regressions cover local boundary-piece transfers
and uploads to a second leecher, hidden-directory attributes, restart, live/paused selection migration,
vectored writes, storage handoff, promotion failure, reserved names, shared-folder isolation, recheck,
folder/single-file moves and loaded/unloaded Keep/Delete removal. Default application build/test/clippy
passed; optional storage-middleware compilation was blocked offline by an uncached lru dependency.
Windows storage safety (2026-10-30): `safe_path.rs` sanitizes each torrent path component before joining it, including reserved device names and a 255 UTF-16-unit cap. Metadata rejects case-insensitive aliases after sanitization; default subfolders and regex paths use the same mapping. The application parser calls this exported mapping for Files, missing-file checks, moves and deletion. `ManagedTorrent::storage_full` inspects the original typed I/O error chain, preserving Windows disk-full classification across engine error context. Local regressions cover actual safe filenames, alias rejection, moves/deletion and an injected disk-full write in a local TCP swarm.

| **SOCKS5 proxy login and local bypass**: decode escaped credentials before peer authentication, optionally bypass private/loopback/link-local peers and HTTP trackers, and omit credentials from parse errors | `librqbit/src/stream_connect.rs`, `session.rs` | The shared proxy setting can route outgoing TCP peers with optional login while preserving explicit local-address bypass. The application disables uTP; DHT and UDP trackers remain direct. |

| **Per-file unfinished markers** (2026-10-30): optional filesystem factory flag, original metadata names, selection/part-file migration and per-file publication | `librqbit/src/storage/filesystem/{fs,opened_file,sparse,mod}.rs`, `torrent_state/{initializing,live/mod}.rs` | New files use .!fx until verified complete; storage handoff, restart, moves and removal retain the physical name. Temporary names fit the Windows component limit; normal/marker aliases are rejected. Publication uses a non-replacing rename, reopens read-only and propagates failures to torrent error state. Defaults retain ordinary filenames. |
| **Extra trackers during magnet resolution** (2026-10-30): merge AddTorrentOptions.trackers for magnets as well as torrent bytes | `librqbit/src/session.rs` | Global extra trackers can find metadata for magnets lacking their own working tracker, while original magnet trackers remain present. |

| **Live weekly blocklist refresh** (2026-10-30) | librqbit/src/session.rs, ip_ranges.rs, torrent_state/live/mod.rs | SessionOptions.blocklist_url still loads the initial list; a session-cancelled task reloads weekly and atomically replaces ranges under a short read/write lock. Incoming/outgoing admission reads the current list. Failed or empty loads retain existing ranges; HTTP requests time out after 60 seconds. Local file URLs and gzip use the existing reader. |
